article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Hybrid
Genetics: Legion OG × Pestilence
Breeder: Inkognyto Genetics, formerly Illuminati Seeds
THC Content: 20%
CBD Content: Typically low
Terpene Profile: caryophyllene , myrcene , limonene
Primary Flavors: Skunk, fuel, earth, pine, spice, sweet fruit
Flowering Time (Indoor): about 9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: late September through October
Indoor Yield: Above average
Outdoor Yield: Above average
Grow Difficulty: Easy to intermediate

Kamikaze comes from a period of cannabis breeding when pungency, vigor, and raw potency often mattered more than dessert names or exotic color. Its genetic foundation is built around Massachusetts Super Skunk , OG-influenced material, West Coast Dawg, and repeated Pestilence influence, giving the cultivar an old-school personality that is noticeably different from modern candy-dominant marijuana. Expect aggressive skunk, fuel, soil, pine, and sharp chemical notes rather than a soft fruit-and-cream bouquet. Healthy examples can produce large, heavily frosted flowers on vigorous plants that stretch into the medium-to-tall range.

Confusion surrounding the name makes genetic verification especially important. Other unrelated weed strains called Kamikaze have been described as White Widow × Jack Herer , while autoflower breeders have also used the same title for completely different crosses. The cultivar covered here is the Inkognyto Genetics version descended from the breeder’s older Illuminati Seeds work. Inkognyto’s current catalog continues to sell Kamikaze and identifies its ancestry through Massachusetts Super Skunk, Pestilence, Abusive OG, West Coast Dog, and OGers genetics.
Genetics and Lineage

The simplest way to understand the pedigree is Legion OG × Pestilence. Legion OG itself combines Massachusetts Super Skunk with Pestilence, meaning the second Pestilence pairing reinforces an already important part of the family tree. The resulting genetic structure can be written as (Massachusetts Super Skunk × Pestilence) × Pestilence. Inkognyto’s current breeder catalog expands Pestilence through Abusive OG, West Coast Dog, and OGers material, revealing just how heavily OG, Chemdawg , and skunk ancestry influences the plant.

That repeated back influence helps explain the cultivar’s distinctive personality. Massachusetts Super Skunk contributes aggressive skunk character and strong vegetative growth, while the Pestilence side introduces a darker mixture of OG fuel, earth, funk, and potency. Rather than combining unrelated parents simply to create novelty, Kamikaze concentrates related traits through the pedigree. The result is a marijuana plant geared toward vigorous growth, substantial resin coverage, and a penetrating smell that can become difficult to conceal late in flowering.
Effects and Experience

The experience can initially feel more mentally active than the genetic background might suggest. A moderate amount may produce a quick change in mood, increased sensory intensity, and a clear euphoric push before physical relaxation becomes dominant. Thoughts can feel faster or more engaging during the opening phase, which makes music, conversation, gaming, or creative activities particularly immersive. For some consumers, the mental lift remains functional; for others, stronger flower can become distracting once the THC builds.

Physical effects tend to arrive progressively rather than all at once. Warmth can spread through the shoulders and limbs while muscular tension becomes less noticeable, eventually replacing the sharper cerebral edge with a heavier state. Larger doses are considerably less forgiving. Strong examples may produce pronounced lethargy, impaired short-term memory, heavy eyelids, or a desire to remain seated. Dry mouth and dry eyes are common THC-related drawbacks, while excessive intake can produce dizziness or anxiety in sensitive consumers. Because no standardized breeder THC figure exists, the laboratory label on the actual flower remains more useful than a generic strain percentage.
Medical Benefits

Kamikaze has not been evaluated as an individual cultivar in controlled medical trials, so medical benefits should not be presented as proven strain-specific outcomes. Its combination of THC-dominant effects and late-session physical relaxation may nevertheless explain why some medical marijuana consumers seek comparable chemotypes for temporary relief from discomfort, poor appetite, stress, or trouble winding down. The transition from an initially brighter mental state toward heavier relaxation may be particularly appealing to patients who want something less immediately sedating than a traditional nighttime indica.

Potency also requires caution in medical use. Higher THC intake can worsen anxiety, dizziness, rapid heart rate, or cognitive impairment, especially among people with limited tolerance. Terpenes may influence aroma and potentially modify the overall cannabis experience, but there is not enough human evidence to treat a proposed terpene profile as a prescription for a medical condition. Patients should rely on the cannabinoid and terpene analysis from their specific batch and discuss cannabis use with a knowledgeable healthcare professional when medications or significant health conditions are involved.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Subtle is not the word for this cultivar. Breaking apart mature flower can release a forceful mixture of skunk musk, petroleum, damp soil, pepper, and sharp pine. Beneath that heavier foundation, certain plants reveal sweeter notes that can resemble sour candy, overripe fruit, or a faint citrus edge. The contrast between sweetness and dirty skunk funk gives the aroma considerably more complexity than a conventional gas strain.

Combustion or vaporization tends to emphasize the earthy and spicy side first. Pepper, woody pine, and OG-like fuel can coat the palate before a sweeter skunk character emerges on the exhale. A properly cured batch may retain that pungency for several minutes after consumption. Because no breeder-certified terpene analysis is available, assigning a fixed dominant terpene would be misleading; however, the pepper, citrus, pine, and earthy characteristics are consistent with compounds such as caryophyllene, limonene, pinene, and myrcene appearing in varying proportions.
Growing Information

Inkognyto Genetics currently describes Kamikaze as a medium-to-tall feminized plant with above-average yield and a flowering period of 63 days or longer. That roughly nine-week schedule makes it relatively manageable for a vigorous OG/skunk-derived hybrid. Plants can establish strong vertical growth, so topping or early canopy training is useful indoors where ceiling height is limited. Spreading branches before flowering also improves light penetration as bud sites begin stacking along the upper canopy.

Flower production can become substantial, making branch support worthwhile during the final weeks. Strong airflow is equally important because large, tightly grouped flowers can trap moisture when humidity remains high. Its breeder-described vigor gives the cultivar some flexibility, but growers should still watch nutrition closely during rapid development; OG-heavy genetics can occasionally display sensitivity or elevated magnesium and calcium demands under intense lighting. Outdoors, ample root space allows the medium-to-tall structure to expand significantly. A warm, dry finish to the season is preferable, especially as dense resinous flowers approach maturity.
FAQ
What are the genetics of the Kamikaze strain?

The Inkognyto Genetics version is Legion OG × Pestilence. Legion OG combines Massachusetts Super Skunk with Pestilence, giving the fuller pedigree of (Massachusetts Super Skunk × Pestilence) × Pestilence.
Who bred Kamikaze?
This version was created by Illuminati Seeds, the breeder now operating as Inkognyto Genetics. Inkognyto continues to list Kamikaze in its current seed catalog.
Is Kamikaze indica or sativa?

Kamikaze is best classified as a hybrid. Its OG, Super Skunk, and Dawg-derived ancestry can produce substantial physical relaxation, although the beginning of the experience may feel mentally stimulating or euphoric.
What does Kamikaze weed taste like?

The flavor generally leans toward skunk, fuel, earthy spice, pine, and OG funk, sometimes accompanied by sweeter fruit or citrus notes. Its pungent character is one of the cultivar’s most distinguishing qualities.
How long does Kamikaze take to flower?

The breeder currently lists flowering at approximately 63 days or longer. Growers should expect roughly nine weeks indoors, although individual plants may need additional time depending on phenotype and environmental conditions.
Final Thoughts on Kamikaze

Kamikaze represents a different branch of cannabis breeding from today’s fruit-heavy and dessert-focused market. Its appeal rests on concentrated skunk, OG, and Dawg genetics, with repeated Pestilence influence reinforcing the pungent traits that define the family. Strong vegetative growth, above-average production, considerable resin, and a penetrating fuel-and-skunk aroma make the plant particularly interesting for growers who value classic marijuana characteristics.

Just as importantly, provenance matters with this strain. Several unrelated cannabis cultivars share the Kamikaze name, so describing every one as White Widow × Jack Herer—or treating every Kamikaze product as genetically identical—creates unnecessary confusion. For the Inkognyto Genetics original covered here, Legion OG × Pestilence is the appropriate lineage. That pedigree produces a vigorous, unapologetically funky hybrid with enough cerebral energy to keep the beginning lively and enough physical weight to give the finish considerably more force.
